name: Jeshua
overview: Jeshua is a male Levite noted for being among the descendants of Hodaviah who returned to Judah after the Babylonian captivity. He is identified as a son of Hodaviah and is possibly a peer or brother of Kadmiel. His role is significant within the post-exilic community as a Levite reestablishing worship and service in Judah.
namesAndTitles: The name Jeshua means 'YHWH saves,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning connected to God's saving work. This proper name is recorded in Ezra 2:40 and carries the significance of divine salvation, common among post-exilic leaders.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Jeshua as a descendant of Hodaviah and the father of Jozabad. He is also noted as a peer or brother of Kadmiel, situating him within a specific Levitical family line involved in the restoration period.
scriptureSignificance: Jeshua's importance lies in his role as a Levite whose descendants returned to Judah after captivity, highlighting the restoration of the Levitical priestly service in the post-exilic community. His mention alongside Hodaviah and Kadmiel underscores the continuity of priestly families dedicated to temple service. Additionally, as the father of Jozabad, Jeshua contributes to the lineage sustaining the religious leadership in the reestablished Jewish community.
